historical_claims.anchor: In The Amazing Spider-Man number one hundred forty-nine, published in 1975, the Jackal's experiments
The clone who had survived became Ben Reilly, named for Uncle Ben and Aunt May's maiden name.
The 1990s storyline developed the terrible possibility that Peter was the clone and Ben the original.
Marvel's published character history of Ben Reilly traces how the saga eventually revealed Ben to be the clone, with Norman Osborn having manipulated the evidence and participants.
Ben dies while saving Peter, his body degenerating and resolving the biological question.
Peter Parker and Mary Jane Watson married in Amazing Spider-Man Annual number twenty-one in 1987.
Then comes One More Day, the four-part 2007 storyline involving The Amazing Spider-Man, Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man, and The Sensational Spider-Man.
The story was written by J. Michael Straczynski, with Joe Quesada deeply involved as writer and artist.

description: Traces the Clone Saga, Peter and Mary Jane’s marriage, and One More Day, exploring the editorial tension between allowing a superhero to mature and preserving a familiar status quo.
